title: Father, uncle, early records, Papa Celestan and Buddy Bolden
summary: Rose names his father, says his uncle bought the early jazz records and knew musicians, and recalls Papa Celestan's band playing at the house.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: My father's name was Lascaux. Oh, no, his first name? Joseph. Joseph, I see.
And, uh, you had an uncle you told me about who was a musical lover.
And did you go to hear music with him?

Uh, no, but he was the one who brought, who bought most of the records that came into the house. Mm-hm. And, uh, uh, of course we had all the early jazz records, largely because of the fact that he knew the musicians himself, and, uh, and I came to know many of the musicians when I was very young. I remember, for example, some social function that went on in the house when I was very young, for which Papa Celestan's band was hired. And, uh, while I don't remember who the individual musicians were, my first recollection of Celestan comes from the time when I was about five years old, during which time he played in the house. Yeah. What about Buddy Bolden? Well, of course, uh, uh, let's see, I guess it was Fred Ramsey that interviewed me on tape about Bolden, and this, uh, involved a trip that I made with my uncle to, uh, Jackson, Louisiana, to the State Mental Hospital. And, uh, as I understood it at the time, I was just twelve years old then, but that he was making an exploratory trip to find out whether Bolden would either be able to perform again or possibly record, I don't know exactly. But, uh, it turned out to be a futile trip, because, uh, I did have the opportunity to see and meet Bolden, but, uh, I believe he was pretty far gone by that time.
